Q7. Which of the following is the appropriate description of the “selection sort” algorithm?

options.text:
An intermediate reference value is determined, and then the elements are divided into
two groups of “larger” values and “smaller” values. This operation is recursively
repeated.

Each set of elements extracted at regular intervals is sorted, and then the interval is
further decreased. The operation is repeatedly performed until the interval becomes 1.

then the largest value of the unsorted elements is determined and swapped for the
second-to-the-last element. This operation is repeated in the same way.

Two adjacent elements are repeatedly compared and swapped if the first element is
larger than the second. This operation is repeated until all elements are arranged in an
orderly fashion.

Q31. Which of the following refers to a technique that is used in a credential stuffing attack?

options.text:
Focusing on the case where there are users that set a word from the dictionary as their
password, selecting one (1) user ID as the target of the attack, and attempting to log in
using words in the dictionary and their combinations as the password

ignored.
Q45. Which of the following is the most appropriate description of a system auditor?

options.text:
The entire audit interview must be conducted by one (1) system auditor, because
discrepancies may occur in the record if multiple auditors are involved.

information obtained from the department being audited during the audit interview.

auditor within the department being audited.

questions.promptText: Q49. Which of the following is an explanation of diversity management?

options.text:

questions.promptText:
Q50. In innovation theory, consumers are classified into five (5) groups innovators, early
adopters, early majority, late majority, and laggards according to the timing of their
purchase of a new product. Which of the following is the appropriate explanation of the
early adopters?

options.text:
A group that accepts a new product, service, or other such offering at an early phase, has
a large impact on consumers, is sensitive to trends, and makes decisions after collecting
information themselves

A group that accepts a new product, service, or other such offering at the soonest phase
without worrying about risks

A group that is skeptical about the adoption of a new product or new technology and
only adopts it after seeing it being adopted by most people around them

A group that is the most conservative, has limited interest in movements in society and
tends to adopt new trends only after they become common or, in some cases, remains
firm in refusing their adoption

A technology for managing all of a company’s relationships and interactions with

A type of software that organizations use to manage day-to-day business activities such
as accounting, procurement, project management, risk management and compliance, and
supply chain operations

Company B runs several web services. Mr. Y is a software engineer in the company. He was
directed to develop a feature that prevents web service users from setting weak passwords.
Mr. Y investigated and found that “Password Entropy” is the important factor for the
password strength.
Password entropy measures the strength of a password based on the difficulty of cracking
the password through guessing or a brute-force attack. The entropy of a password is typically
based on the type of characters used—lowercase letters, uppercase letters, numerical digits,
or special characters—and the length of the password or total number of characters.
Password entropy formula:
You can measure the entropy of a password in bits using the following formula:
E = ⌊L ×Log (R)⌋
2
In this formula:
- E denotes the password entropy
- R denotes the possible range of character types in the password
- L denotes the number of characters in the password (its length)
- Log answers the question, "to what power 2 must be raised to equal this number"
2
- ⌊X⌋ denotes the greatest integer N such that N ≤ X
The following totals show the breakdown for each character set as they appear on a typical
American QWERTY keyboard:
Lowercase letters (a–z) = 26.
Uppercase letters (A–Z) = 26.
Numerical digits (0–9) = 10.
Special characters (!, @, #, $, %, ^, etc.) = 32.
The password vfssxfrb has a pool of 26 characters (lowercase letters);
Changing the password to JAAdMAdE would increase the pool to 52 characters (lowercase
letters and uppercase letters);
Changing it further to u7aHqsbt would increase the pool to 62 characters (lowercase letters,
uppercase letters along with numbers) and
Finally, Re*ct7$% has a pool of 26 + 26 + 10 + 32 = 94 characters (lowercase letters,

uppercase letters, numbers, and special characters).
In our example:
• For vfssxfrb, we have R = 26 and L = 8; thus,
E = ⌊8 × log (26) ⌋ ≈ ⌊8 × 4.700⌋ ≈ ⌊37.60⌋ = 37 bits
2
• For JAAdMAdE, we have R = 52 and L = 8; thus,
E = ⌊8 × log (52) ⌋ ≈ ⌊8 × 5.700⌋ ≈ ⌊45.60⌋ = 45 bits
2
• For u7aHqsbt, we have R = 62 and L = 8; thus,
E = ⌊8 × log (62) ⌋ ≈ ⌊8 × 5.954⌋ ≈ ⌊47.63⌋ = 47 bits
2
• For Re*ct7$%, we have R = 94 and L = 8; thus,
E = ⌊8 × log (94) ⌋ ≈ ⌊8 × 6.555⌋ ≈ ⌊52.44⌋ = 52 bits
2

uppercase letters. L = 9), the password entropy is ____ ___ bits.
